scope.classification: These 16 repository-defined schemas comprise core fund/NAV/family/facts/quality, fund-related provenance and operational/review evidence, official source documents/disclosures, current/monthly/book facts, portfolios, distributions, overlap and calendar/rolling research. Includes fund-related receipts/configurations/review actors by deliberate schema-level policy; this does not make raw internal evidence a public UI export. mf.source_metadata has freeform error/notes/request_url and mf_review/mf_fact_review contain actor/caller/idempotency evidence: fresh live preparation must attest data-schema custody and absence of credentials/unrelated personal records before granting, not assert that static SQL proves their contents safe.
scope.excluded: No pg_catalog/information_schema/public or arbitrary prefix-matching schemas; no passwords/private role/function settings/DSNs/IAM/customer records. No global pg_read_all_data role, role membership, superuser, BYPASSRLS, schema CREATE, sequence mutation, function EXECUTE, source DML/DDL, admin-review mutations or grant option.
scope.lifetime: Persistent table-level SELECT, all existing/future columns and all rows exposed by approved objects; not temporary job-only scope. The existing shared reader's ALL consumers receive these rights. No identity creation or role switch. Existing RLS is not disabled/bypassed; any RLS target blocks an unrestricted-all-rows claim and live application pending explicit disposition.
scope.future_objects: For the fixed existing creator mfdata_admin, schema-local ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES GRANT SELECT ON TABLES; no global defaults. Future table/view columns inherit table-level SELECT. Objects created by other roles do NOT inherit this creator's defaults. An entirely new schema or different creator must be enrolled by its provisioning composition, not silently claimed covered. That is a schema-ownership boundary, not per-field entitlement.
scope.future_trust_boundary: Trusted administrators must keep these domain schemas free of secrets/unrelated personal data and unapproved foreign tables. PostgreSQL table default privileges include foreign tables; there is no relkind filter in ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES. Current foreign tables fail admission; future provisioning must reject them before commit. No claim of universal prevention against an owner creating arbitrary content or revoking access later. No event trigger/admin policy framework is introduced here.

plan_and_exact_delta.input: Complete sealed catalogue document, no direct source rows. Strict keys/types/unique canonical numeric ACL atoms, canonical object/schema/column identities and complete state sets. Need mf schema plus existing owner/reader. Present optional schemas listed explicitly, absent schemas reported NOT_ENROLLED rather than created/assumed deployed. All target schemas/relations owned by fixed owner; reader non-elevated/no memberships/no write or grant-option capabilities. Current foreign/unsupported relation kinds or RLS reject. All existing unrelated state, roles, memberships, function/sequence/database ACLs preserved.
plan_and_exact_delta.grant_operations: Only missing direct owner non-grantable USAGE on present approved schemas, missing direct owner non-grantable relation SELECT for all present r/p/v/m objects, and missing schema-local owner/default r SELECT. Deterministically enumerated object grants avoid silently sweeping a concurrently created unapproved object. This is mechanics, not a user-selectable object/column allowlist. No revokes in forward apply. All source rows, view/function definitions, owners, object/column identities/types/options unchanged.
plan_and_exact_delta.default_identity: Compare default ACL records by unique (creator_oid,namespace_oid,object_type), complete atoms retained. The catalog row OID for a newly created default ACL is server-allocated and cannot be predicted; exclude ONLY pg_default_acl row OID from semantic comparison, document this normalization and test new/default-existing/global cases. Do not ignore role/schema/object OIDs or grantor/grant option mismatches.
plan_and_exact_delta.capability_projection: Every target table SELECT and every live column SELECT become true; all write/grant-option flags and other capabilities remain exactly as before. Preserve preexisting table/column grants from every grantor. Add only missing fixed-owner read atoms; default rows create only matching scoped owner/schema/type entries. After snapshot must equal exact projected full canonical state with only documented default-row-OID normalization.
plan_and_exact_delta.plan_fingerprint: Plan contains fixed profile hash, catalogue before hash, exact full expected-after hash, present/absent schema coverage, full missing grant/default delta and deterministic SQL operations. A single-use deepcopied envelope binds the exact plan plus exclusive administrative window and schema-custody attestations. Hash equality is NOT evidence of human approval; final G5 runtime boundary must obtain direct exact-input approval and persist intent before invoking this dormant module.

executor.bounds: One already-connected autocommit/idle direct-owner connection, main thread/no existing process timer. Fresh single-use binding consumed before first database I/O. Whole 15s SIGALRM/monotonic wall includes capture, validation, grants, verification, COMMIT and final verification; five-second statement/lock settings and original server transaction timeout. No connect/reconnect, SET ROLE, retries, timeout/resource raises, arbitrary callbacks or more SQL after spent wall.
executor.sequence: Validate envelope/window/attestations/pure plan first; arm wall; BEGIN READ COMMITTED READ WRITE; fixed SET LOCAL statement_timeout5s/lock_timeout5s/transaction_timeout15s/search_pathpg_catalog/timezoneUTC; direct identity/context check; fresh complete before-state equals approved catalogue; issue ONLY generated missing grants/defaults; new READ COMMITTED full snapshot equals exact projected state; COMMIT once; fresh final full snapshot equals expected; emit finite COMMITTED_VERIFIED result with profile/before/after/plan hashes and effective coverage. All window checks before writes and COMMIT; no availability/financial/runtime acceptance inferred.
executor.concurrency: G5 must attest an exclusive ACL/schema/role/provisioning administrative window. Whole-state comparisons detect observed drift, not prevent arbitrary administrative races. No new manual AccessExclusive recursive relation locks: this is a schema-level access policy, not a frozen two-object financial projection edit. PostgreSQL GRANT may take its normal catalogue/relation locks and affect concurrency; no zero-availability-impact claim. No guarantees after COMMIT against an administrator changing privileges or placing private data in an enrolled schema.
executor.failures: Before COMMIT: sole rollback only if begun and budget remains; rollback failure/timeout produces ABORT_UNCONFIRMED or WALL_ABORT_UNCONFIRMED, not the original-error-only label. Spent wall means no more I/O, connection teardown by transport is not proof of confirmed rollback. A COMMIT exception is COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and no rollback/retry/reversal. Returned COMMIT followed by missing/failed final evidence is COMMITTED_UNVERIFIED and no automatic reversal. Redacted fixed-stage errors only, no SQL/settings/DSN or provider exception text.
executor.reversal: Prearm a NONEXECUTABLE exact missing-grant/default delta receipt. Do not add an automatic revoke path or implement a generic role-reset installer. A separate newly authorized exact reversal must preserve all preexisting table/column/default grants and consider any future objects that inherited defaults; reverting defaults does NOT revoke already-created objects. Forward code receipt labels this explicitly and never claims full recovery from default reversal alone.
